clue.text: Maybe the Communist Manifesto — with Lenin's lead — set rebels off?

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
Lenin's lead is the opening letter of the revolutionary's name

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool

explanation.surface: A political tract, steered by Lenin, sets the rebels going in revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges L (from 'Lenin's lead') with SET REBELS. The question mark flags the definition by example: the Manifesto sold in vast numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Communist Manifesto has sold millions of copies, an example of a hugely popular book.

clue.text: American novelist another one dumped in the water

indicators.note: dumped means thrown out, so one name is removed from the other

parts.note: John Steinbeck, author of The Grapes of Wrath
Gertrude Stein, a second American writer

explanation.surface: An American writer throws a rival novelist into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumped' takes STEIN (Gertrude Stein, 'another one') out of STEINBECK. A beck is a northern English word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A beck is a brook or mountain stream, a stretch of running water in northern England.

clue.text: Caviare producer cuts time for operator

indicators.note: cuts means removes, so a letter is taken out of the fish

parts.note: the sturgeon is the fish whose roe is caviare

explanation.surface: A caviare supplier trims the time it needs to serve the operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' removes T (time) from STURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations, so an operator in the medical sense.

clue.text: Leicester cop drafted into NKVD, perhaps

indicators.note: drafted as in redrawn or recast, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool

explanation.surface: A Leicester policeman is drafted into the Soviet security service.
explanation.definitionFit: The NKVD was the Soviet political police force under Stalin, an example of a covert state enforcement agency.

clue.text: Landlord's worrying silence over second instalment of rent

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part sits above the second
worrying in the sense of disturbing or shaking up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool

indicators.note: the second instalment of the word rent is its second letter

explanation.surface: A landlord's alarming silence hangs over the second payment of rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' rearranges SILENCE to LICENSE, then 'over' places it above E, the second letter of 'rent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord holds the licence to sell alcohol, so is the licence-holder of the premises.

clue.text: Praise gained from trade association journal upon end of display

indicators.note: in a down clue upon means placed above the following pieces

parts.note: the EU, the European Union, is a trading bloc
a log is a daily record or journal

indicators.note: end of the word display is its final letter

explanation.surface: Praise taken from a trade body's magazine after a show closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing full of praise, often for someone who has died.

clue.text: Smart hippie girl's losing weight

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the girl

parts.note: chick is dated slang for a young woman, as hippies used it
K stands for kilogram, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A trendy hippie girl looks smarter after losing some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes K (kilo, 'weight') off CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a synonym for stylish and elegant, matching smart in the fashionable sense.

clue.text: Bent husband to reveal private number

parts.note: to air something is to make it public
a PIN is a personal identification number, kept secret

explanation.surface: A crooked husband discloses a secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is bent into a U shape, and the word is used for a sharply bending road.

clue.text: Ruling cabal's first error — to tangle with leaders of union and demonstrators

indicators.note: the first of the word cabal is its opening letter
tangle means the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool
taken as written for the letter pool

indicators.note: leaders of the words union and demonstrators are their first letters

explanation.surface: A ruling clique's first blunder is to clash with union chiefs and protesters.
explanation.walkthrough: C from 'cabal's first'; 'tangle with' rearranges ERROR, TO, U and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's ruling is an order issued by a court, a legal decision.

clue.text: Growth on seafood a threat to the harvest?

parts.note: a corn is a hard growth of skin on the foot
a cockle is an edible shellfish

explanation.surface: Something growing on shellfish might endanger the crop.
explanation.walkthrough: The corncockle is a weed of cornfields whose seeds are poisonous, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple-flowered weed infests grain crops and its toxic seeds once contaminated the harvested wheat.

clue.text: Off and on, admire our Maker?

indicators.note: off and on means taking every other letter of the words admire our, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Now and then we stop to admire our Creator.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of ADMIRE OUR give the French word for God; the clue's 'our' serves both the surface and the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieu is French for God, the Creator and Maker of all things.

clue.text: See the places reassigned in race

indicators.note: reassigned means the letters are given new positions

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool

explanation.surface: Look at how the finishing places were reallocated in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race over fences, or an athletics race with hurdles and water jumps.

clue.text: Markova's spring and summer in Paris with Jack?

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
été is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: A ballerina's leap, and a summer in Paris with a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Alicia Markova was a celebrated British ballerina, so her 'spring' is a ballet leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet jump from one foot to the other, the kind of leap a ballerina makes.

clue.text: Perhaps clip joint's near top of town, see?

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: top of the word town is its first letter

parts.note: to spot is to see or notice

explanation.surface: A clip joint sits near the top of town, you see.
explanation.walkthrough: A clip joint is a nightclub that overcharges its customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip joint is a type of nightclub, so an example of a late-evening entertainment venue.

clue.text: Most impressive gallery in Sweden is situated on edge of Trelleborg

indicators.note: in a down clue on means this part sits above the next

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
the Tate is a London art gallery
lies means is located

indicators.note: edge of the word Trelleborg is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sweden's finest gallery stands on the outskirts of the port of Trelleborg.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London gallery, not a Swedish one; Trelleborg is a Swedish port that only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateliest is the superlative of stately, meaning grand and dignified in appearance.

clue.text: 'La Mer', say, only in unusual tempo

indicators.note: in means the sole word goes inside the shuffled letters
unusual signals that the letters of tempo are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool
one means single or sole, as in the one person

explanation.surface: Debussy's 'La Mer' is played only at an unusual tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the tempo letters into T plus POEM, with the sole word slotted in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Debussy's La Mer is an orchestral work evoking the sea, an example of symphonic programme music.

clue.text: Amount made by returning ingredient for cheese?

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: rennet curdles milk in cheesemaking

explanation.surface: How much money a cheesemaker earns from recycling an ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound sum of money is a specific amount, so the slang term fits loosely.

clue.text: Hackney is said to be attractive

indicators.note: is said means the cab's name is spoken

parts.note: a hackney is a horse-drawn cab for hire, such as a hansom

explanation.surface: Hackney, the London borough, is reputed to be a good-looking place.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London district but means a hired carriage; the hansom was a two-wheeled cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-looking people are described as handsome, a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Mark's two spots of legerdemain amuse

parts.note: a tick is a mark on a page

indicators.note: two spots of the word legerdemain means its first two letters

explanation.surface: Mark's two tricks of sleight of hand entertain the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two spots of' takes LE, the first two letters of 'legerdemain'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tickle someone is to amuse or delight them, as in tickled pink.

clue.text: Key to unlock circular saw was right twisted and unused

indicators.note: unlock means opening up, so the letters are freed and rearranged
unused means these letters are left out
twisted means the word was and the letter for right are turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The key to a circular saw was wrongly turned and never used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns WAS R to RSAW; 'unused' takes it out of CIRCULAR SAW, leaving CIRCULA, which 'to unlock' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucial means vital or decisive, the same sense as key in a key factor.

clue.text: Spin wicked tale about human

indicators.note: about means the tale wraps around the turned word

parts.note: a fable is a short moral tale

indicators.note: spin means turn round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ill can mean evil or wicked, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: Spinning a wicked yarn about humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' looks like an anagram signal but here only turns the wicked word round before the tale wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being human means being liable to make mistakes, as in to err is human.

clue.text: Tap phone of sailor getting rings — it's an alarming thing

parts.note: to bug a phone is to tap it
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
O is shaped like a ring, so two rings give OO

explanation.surface: A sailor's phone is tapped and he gets calls — a frightening business.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugaboo is a bogey or bugbear, an object of fear or dread.

clue.text: Surge precipitous (not half!) on vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue on means this part sits above the vessel
not half means the first half of the word is dropped

parts.note: abrupt means sudden or steep, like precipitous
an urn is a vase or container

explanation.surface: A steep rise, not half, on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops ABR, the first half of ABRUPT, leaving UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an upward movement or improvement, like a surge in sales.

clue.text: Tread softly on boat — it helps with starting

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the first piece follows the second

parts.note: a launch is a motorboat
to pad is to walk with soft steps

explanation.surface: Tiptoe aboard a boat, a help when getting under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket rises from its pad at liftoff, so the platform helps with starting a flight.

clue.text: Century's a long time in prison

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for century
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A hundred years is a long stretch behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is an enclosure that confines, used figuratively for a jail.

clue.text: Fell race?

definitions.meaning: a fell is an animal's hide or skin
to race is to hurry along at speed

explanation.surface: A race over the fells, the hill country of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal hide, as is a fell; to pelt along is to race.

clue.text: Italian's on extra leave

indicators.note: in an across clue on means this piece comes after the other

parts.note: EX is a short form of extra, as in ex-directory
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: An Italian on extra holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to depart or go out, a verb sense matching leave.

clue.text: Beeb labours endlessly breaking down community jargon

indicators.note: breaking down signals the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of labours is cut off

explanation.surface: The BBC toils on without end at breaking down jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a nickname for the BBC. 'endlessly' trims LABOURS to LABOUR; 'breaking down' rearranges it with BEEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Euro-jargon from the European Community's bureaucracy is mocked as babble, meaningless official talk.

clue.text: Work the checkout?

definitions.meaning: to work soil is to plough or cultivate it
the cash register at a shop checkout

explanation.surface: A question about serving shoppers at the supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to work it, and a till is the cash register at a checkout.

clue.text: No tweezers used to make ersatz snuff

indicators.note: used as in put to work differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool

explanation.surface: No tweezers needed to make a substitute snuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Sneezewort is a yarrow whose dried leaves were once used as a snuff substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried leaves of this plant were powdered and sniffed to provoke sneezing, a stand-in for tobacco.
